identity.title: Imaging [CI] around HD 131835: reinterpreting young debris discs with protoplanetary disc levels of CO gas as shielded secondary discs
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: New ALMA observations are presented of HD131835 that detect $\sim 3 \times 10^{-3}$ M$_\oplus$ of C$^0$, the majority 40-200au from the star, in sufficient quantity to shield the previously detected CO.

evidence.quote: HD 131835 is a 15-16 Myr old (cite: 2002AJ....124.1670M; 2012ApJ...746..154P) A-type star located at a distance[^3] of 145$\pm$9 pc
HD 131835 is a 15-16 Myr old (cite: 2002AJ....124.1670M; 2012ApJ...746..154P) A-type star located at a distance[^3] of 145$\pm$9 pc

question.value: Can debris discs with protoplanetary-disc levels of CO be secondary (shielded by accumulated neutral carbon) rather than hybrid, tested with new ALMA [CI] and continuum data of HD 131835 plus a semi-analytic model?

evidence.quote: Here we show that both the dust and gas in such systems could instead be secondary, with the high CO content caused by accumulation of neutral carbon (C$^0$) that shields CO from photodissociating
HD 131835 was observed by ALMA in band 8 on 22$^{\rm nd}$ March 2017

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 3 continuum SPWs (128 channels, centred 480.201, 482.159, 494.201 GHz); 1 line SPW at 492.160651 GHz, 488.281 kHz (0.297 km/s) over 3840 channels

evidence.quote: with a higher spectral resolution of 488.281 kHz (0.297 km/s at the rest frenquency of the line) over 3840 channels
